proposed_widenings.name: smite_activation family
proposed_widenings.justification: Shining Smite (and smite spells generally) fire as a Bonus Action taken AFTER a weapon hit already resolved. The immediate 2d6 Radiant damage applies to that triggering hit—not to a new spell-originated attack roll, and not to subsequent hits. No existing family captures 'post-hit activation: one-time damage on the triggering hit + concentration-based ongoing effects on the target.' The activation family requires a new attack roll from the spell itself. The ongoing_effect family's damage_on_hit operation fires when the caster makes subsequent attack hits against the attachment, not on the triggering hit.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The target hit by the strike takes an extra 2d6 Radiant damage from the attack. Until the spell ends, the target sheds Bright Light in a 5-foot radius, attack rolls against it have Advantage, and it can't benefit from the Invisible condition.

proposed_widenings.name: CastingTime: bonus_action_conditional (after-hit trigger)
proposed_widenings.justification: CastingTime's bonus_action variant carries no condition field. Smite spells restrict the bonus action to 'immediately after hitting a creature with a Melee weapon or Unarmed Strike.' This timing constraint is mechanically significant: the hit must resolve first, then the bonus action is available. The closest existing type is reaction with ReactionTrigger, but smite casts are Bonus Actions that consume the bonus-action quota, not the reaction quota.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "which you take immediately after hitting a creature with a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike"

proposed_widenings.name: OngoingOperation: modify_roll_advantage
proposed_widenings.justification: The ongoing effect grants Advantage on attack rolls made against the target. OngoingOperation only supports roll_modifier (numeric delta) and damage_on_hit. There is no advantage/disadvantage variant. The atom modify_roll_advantage exists in v4 as a MasteryEffect, but is not surfaced as a spell OngoingOperation shape. Faerie Fire has the same pattern and would need this widening too.
proposed_widenings.evidence: attack rolls against it have Advantage

proposed_widenings.name: deny_condition_benefit
proposed_widenings.justification: The spell prevents the target from benefiting from the Invisible condition without removing it. The Invisible condition may still be present on the creature; only its mechanical benefits (concealment, attack disadvantage/advantage) are suppressed. remove_condition would be wrong, apply_condition is wrong. No v4 atom covers 'nullify the mechanical benefits of condition X while leaving the condition applied.' The suppress procedure atom is close but is a procedure, not an effect atom on a target.
proposed_widenings.evidence: it can't benefit from the Invisible condition

notes: The smite pattern (bonus action post-hit, damage on triggering hit, then ongoing concentration effects) is shared by Searing Smite, Thunderous Smite, Wrathful Smite, Blinding Smite, and Staggering Smite. A new smite_activation family—or a widening of ongoing_effect to support a 'triggering_hit_damage' initial phase before the ongoing operation begins—would address the entire smite pattern in one widening. The bright-light-shedding effect is omitted from proposed_widenings because it is a presentation/environment effect (caller-owned per ARCHITECTURE.md) whose only mechanically deterministic consequence is the Advantage grant and condition-benefit denial already captured above.
